content.text: In Bangladesh, digital creators face a stark reality: Stripe and PayPal are not options. Your ability to sell [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-sell-ebooks-kenya-which-architecture-actually-works-2|How to]], courses, or templates depends on infrastructure you control. This is not about workarounds—it’s about building a commerce stack that cannot be suspended, restricted, or revoked. COREMERCH provides the [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-art-without-paypal-explained-digital-creators-6|COREMERCH guide to selling]]-stock-photos-without-paypal-4|architecture]]. This analysis compares your real options for sovereign commerce infrastructure, focusing on ownership, payment verification, and delivery automation. We’ll evaluate free tools, paid solutions, and hybrid setups. The goal is clear: to give you a commerce stack that operates on your terms, with no geographic gatekeeping. This is not a temporary fix. It’s a permanent shift to infrastructure sovereignty.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Sovereign Commerce Infrastructure for Digital Creators at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/coremerch-sovereign-stack-deployment-guide-what-nobody-tells-18. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: Sovereign Commerce Infrastructure for Digital Creators

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers

Free tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Google Sheets can form the backbone of a sovereign commerce stack. GitHub Pages provides static hosting, Cloudflare Workers handle backend logic, and Google Sheets stores orders. NOWPayments integrates for crypto payment verification. This setup is free but requires technical assembly. Paid solutions like Shopify or WooCommerce offer convenience but come with platform risk—they can suspend your store. COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit ($197) delivers pre-configured stacks with full ownership. It includes blueprints for five commerce architectures, templates for seven product types, and a scaling playbook. The tradeoff is clear: free tools require time, paid solutions risk suspension, and COREMERCH provides a middle ground—owned infrastructure without the assembly burden.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Free tools and COREMERCH’s stacks are geographically neutral. GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase do not restrict access based on location. Crypto payments via NOWPayments bypass traditional banking rails, eliminating geographic gatekeeping. Shopify and WooCommerce, however, rely on payment gateways that often block countries like Bangladesh. Even if you use a VPN, your store can be suspended if detected. COREMERCH’s architecture is designed for regions where Stripe and PayPal are unavailable. It leverages decentralized payment verification and self-hosted delivery, ensuring your commerce operations are not tied to any single jurisdiction. This is not a workaround—it’s a rearchitecting of your commerce stack for sovereignty.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Crypto payments via NOWPayments confirm within minutes, with a 0.5% fee. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON keep transaction costs under $0.10. Free tools incur no platform fees but require time to configure. Shopify and WooCommerce charge monthly fees plus transaction costs, and their payment gateways often add additional fees. COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit is a one-time $197 investment. It includes pre-configured stacks, eliminating the need for ongoing subscriptions. The real cost comparison is clear: free tools require time, Shopify/WooCommerce risk suspension and fees, and COREMERCH provides owned infrastructure with minimal upfront cost.
Infrastructure sovereignty is not optional—it’s the only way to sell without geographic gatekeeping.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With COREMERCH’s stacks, you own the storefront code, customer list, order history, product files, and wallet addresses. Automation is handled via Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, ensuring instant product delivery upon payment confirmation. Free tools require manual configuration for automation. Shopify and WooCommerce store your data on their servers, and they control the automation logic. If suspended, you lose access to everything. COREMERCH’s architecture ensures you retain full ownership and control. Your commerce stack is deployed to your GitHub or Cloudflare account, and NOWPayments handles payment verification without storing your data. This is infrastructure sovereignty—not renting, but owning.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you have technical skills and time, assemble a free stack using GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments. If you need a pre-configured solution with full ownership, COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit is the clear choice. Shopify and WooCommerce are not viable options for creators in restricted countries. The decision comes down to your tolerance for platform risk and your desire for infrastructure sovereignty. COREMERCH’s stacks are built for creators who prioritize ownership and control. They are pressure-tested against actual payment rejection, currency collapse, and financial isolation. Choose the architecture that aligns with your long-term goals—not just your immediate needs.
What does sovereign commerce infrastructure mean for digital creators?

For digital creators in Bangladesh, COREMERCH’s Complete Builder Kit offers the most sovereign commerce infrastructure. It includes pre-configured stacks, full ownership of all components, and integration with NOWPayments for crypto transactions. Unlike Shopify or WooCommerce, it eliminates platform suspension risk and geographic gatekeeping. Free tools require manual assembly, while COREMERCH provides a ready-to-deploy solution. This is not a temporary fix—it’s a permanent shift to infrastructure sovereignty.
NOWPayments’ 0.5% fee is the lowest cost for decentralized payment verification.

Infrastructure sovereignty is a decision you make once and benefit from permanently. After the stack is deployed under your accounts, no platform decision affects your revenue, your customer list, or your product delivery. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 makes that decision concrete in 48 hours — deployed, tested, and handed off. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you the documentation to make it yourself. Both options are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

1. Choose your hosting: GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. 2. Set up backend logic: Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. 3. Configure order storage: Supabase or Google Sheets. 4. Integrate file delivery: Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. 5. Add payment verification: NOWPayments with webhook automation. 6. Load your products and test end-to-end. 7. Deploy and retain full ownership of your stack.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use COREMERCH’s stacks if I’m not technical?
Yes, the Complete Builder Kit includes pre-configured blueprints and templates. You’ll need basic familiarity with GitHub or Cloudflare, but no advanced coding is required.
What cryptocurrencies does NOWPayments support?
NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoins like USDT. Recommended networks for low fees are BSC, Solana, and TRON.
Do I need to pay monthly fees for COREMERCH’s stacks?
No, COREMERCH’s stacks are a one-time purchase. You own the infrastructure and pay only the 0.5% NOWPayments fee per transaction.
Can Shopify or WooCommerce work in Bangladesh?
Shopify and WooCommerce rely on payment gateways that often block restricted countries. Even with a VPN, your store risks suspension if detected.
What happens if I lose access to my GitHub or Cloudflare account?
Since you own the infrastructure, you can redeploy it to another account. COREMERCH has no access to your stack after delivery.
